# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) before it writes any code. ## Contributing with agents Please use [Agent Traffic Control](https://github.com/ashhart/ATC) before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes. Check the [live agent radar](https://tensorfold.dev/atc) before choosing an issue and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [ATC contributor instructions](docs/atc/SKILL.md). Install or upgrade ATC to 0.9.4 or later, then run from an updated TensorFold clone: ```sh npm install -g github:ashhart/ATC atc check ISSUE --json atc claim ISSUE --json ``` Replace `ISSUE` with the issue number and claim only after a complete check says the work is free. TensorFold enables automatic public check-ins: a successful new claim starts an anonymous session on the radar and returns its `session` number. Keep that number instead of starting a duplicate session. For work already yours, start a session with `atc start ISSUE --json`. Add `--github-name` to `claim` or `start` only if you want your verified GitHub name shown; `--local` keeps a new session on your machine. The board shows the issue, activity state and last check-in; GitHub still associates the verification comment with its author. Check that `publication` is `public`; `unavailable` means the public update failed even if the local claim or session succeeded. Pulse only while the agent is working, before its five-minute check-in expires: ```sh atc pulse ISSUE SESSION working --json atc who path/to/file --json atc overlap --json atc land ISSUE SESSION --json atc release ISSUE --json ``` Use `reviewing` or `blocked` when appropriate, land the session when it stops, and resolve overlaps before opening a pull request. Before opening a pull request, have the agent run the [pull request skill](docs/pr/SKILL.md); agents that support skills can install it as `tensorfold-pull-request`. ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, the small 4-bit checkpoint checked on Metal and a GB10. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. Reviewing or benchmarking TensorFold? [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) covers pinning, signature checks, a container and the tests that need no GPU. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Use the release archive for your CPU: `linux-aarch64` on a GB10, `linux-x86_64` on an x86_64 host. It needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0), providing `libcuda.so.1`. Keep the archive's directories together. Its kernels are built with CUDA 13, so TensorFold refuses an older driver at startup; `nvidia-smi` shows the installed one. See the [CUDA runbook](RUNBOOK.md#linux-and-cuda) for runtime libraries and supported GPUs. ```sh V=1.2.7 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. On Windows with an NVIDIA GPU, follow [the native Windows build guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). Use `tensorfold --help`, `tensorfold capabilities --json` and `tensorfold serve REPO --help` to inspect your binary. You can also serve a complete local checkpoint directory or an existing Hugging Face cache. `tensorfold web [ARGS...]` opens TensorFold Web, a small local web app for picking, running and chatting with models. If it needs installing, an interactive release binary offers to install its matching version with `uv` after you say yes. See [the web launcher](docs/web.md) for manual installation and unattended use. `--parallel N` caps active requests at N; extra requests wait for a free slot. Omitting the flag uses `--parallel auto`, which asks for up to eight streams as memory and the engine allow. An explicit number is refused if the engine cannot fit that many streams. Read the engine's startup capacity line, such as `8 streams at once` on CUDA, for the count it accepted. With API authentication off, `/health` reports `live.connections` as active plus waiting requests and `live.waiting` as the queued count. For example, 8 connections with 4 waiting means 4 active requests. Completing or cancelling an active request frees its slot; cancelling a waiting request removes it from the queue. ## Mac app The [TensorFold desktop workspace](app/README.md) bundles the local engine, model downloads, hardware recommendations, live generation metrics, coding workers and document editing. Download the Apple-silicon [beta 9 DMG](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/tag/v1.0.0-beta.9), or build from [`app/`](app/README.md). The desktop app launches the bundled `tensorfold-native` executable directly. Mobile clients in `app/mobile/` remain preview software. ## TensorFold Starlight (enterprise) [TensorFold Starlight](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight) gives an organisation one governed OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoint for a fleet of TensorFold engines on Macs, Linux GPU servers and Windows machines. It signs people in through the organisation's identity provider (OIDC or SAML, with SCIM provisioning), decides who may use which model and where it runs, places and supervises models on nodes, and accounts for every token. It runs fully offline, or brokers approved frontier providers under the same identity, policy and budgets; [the install guide](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight/blob/main/docs/install.md) covers Docker, Kubernetes and Linux services. Starlight lives in its own repository, [ashhart/tf-starlight](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight): it pins the TensorFold release it is tested with and checks every flag its nodes pass to `tensorfold serve` against that release in CI. Starlight is new: the gates that still need real GPU clusters or identity-provider tenants are listed in [its qualification notes](https://github.com/ashhart/tf-starlight/blob/main/docs/qualification.md). ## Living Weights (experimental) Living Weights teaches a running model new facts in its own weights. Start a Nemotron 3.5 Lightning server with `--slide` and tell it something: each fact that passes the lesson's checks is written into the checkpoint folder's files. It is experimental: related facts can disturb each other, recall drops past a few dozen facts and with thinking on, and learned facts cost some decode speed on a Mac. [Known issues](docs/known-issues.md#living-weights---slide) has the details. ```sh tensorfold pull TensorFold/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit hub="${HF_HUB_CACHE:-${HF_HOME:-$HOME/.cache/huggingface}/hub}/models--TensorFold--NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit" src="$hub/snapshots/$(cat "$hub/refs/main")" mkdir -p ~/models && cp -RL "$src" ~/models/nemotron-living # always teach a copy (umask 077; openssl rand -hex 24 > ~/models/slide-key) # --slide starts only with a key tensorfold serve ~/models/nemotron-living --slide --api-key-file ~/models/slide-key ``` Leave that server running and send a lesson from another terminal: ```sh curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/slide/learn -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/models/slide-key)" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text": "I like blue."}' ``` Send it a document instead and it finds the facts in it and learns them one by one. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/slide` to watch in 3D: the facts, the neurons each one took in the model's layers, the shard files that hold them, and the lesson running now. Learning runs on Apple-silicon Macs and on an NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), and a folder that learned on one serves on the other. On an APFS volume, `cp -cRL` makes a clone that shares the original's data until lessons change it. It rewrites the folder's files: before the first lesson the server keeps the originals in a hidden snapshot, and `tensorfold slide rollback ~/models/nemotron-living` puts them back, undoing every lesson. The [Living Weights guide](docs/living-weights.md) covers the key, teaching files and web pages, omp's `/learn` command, the 3D view, undoing lessons, and what to expect. ## Pick a model These are the native release's serving paths. A recipe may also describe the older Python 0.6.6 engine; use its native section and the current [changes](CHANGELOG.md) together. Hardware below records the documented scope, not an unmeasured minimum. Context, parallel requests, prompt caches and drafters need memory beyond the weights. `tensorfold info REPO` reports the checkpoint's memory floor. Where no RAM capacity is published, inspect that floor before serving a large checkpoint. CUDA release images include sm_80, sm_86, sm_120 and sm_121. The A100 (sm_80) has kernel-check evidence ([#846](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/846)), but no served checkpoint on record, so it is not model-qualified. Nemotron and dense Qwen have NVFP4/FP8 fallback code for sm_80 to sm_89 (#901, #1470); no such model run on sm_80 to sm_89 is recorded. Run a table command after installation. On a Linux archive installation, use the `tensorfold` shell function from Quick start. `REPO@revision` pins a pull; serve the repository name without the revision after pulling it.
